googleAnalytics.title: UTM Campaign Performance — May 1 to June 21, 2026

eventCount.label: Event count
eventCount.definition: Total number of events recorded. An event is any user interaction tracked in GA4 (page views, clicks, scrolls, etc.). Higher event counts indicate more overall engagement from that traffic source.

engagedSessions.label: Engaged sessions
engagedSessions.definition: The number of sessions that lasted longer than 10 seconds, had a conversion event, or had 2 or more screen/page views. This is a quality-over-quantity metric — it filters out bounces and shows sessions where users actually interacted. Note: This metric is an approximation and may differ across GA4 surfaces.

sessions.label: Sessions
sessions.definition: A session is a group of user interactions with your website within a given time frame (default 30 minutes). Each visit starts a new session. This is the broadest traffic metric — all visitors, including bounces.

keyEvents.label: Key events
keyEvents.definition: Events marked as particularly important to your business. Any event can be designated as a key event. These are your conversions — actions like form submissions, purchases, or phone calls. Only 3 key events were recorded across all campaigns in this period.

insights: ai-intent-mmai (outdoor-intent) drives the most traffic — 661 events, 46 sessions (50.5% of all sessions). This is the Sissy Outdoor Furniture AI Intent Data sequence.
customer-sequence-mmai (existing-customers) is second — 421 events, 16 sessions. Strong engagement despite lower volume.
The only 3 key events (conversions) came from direct/organic traffic (Porch+Patio segment with no campaign ID). No UTM-tagged campaign has generated a key event yet.
Engagement rate (engaged sessions / sessions): outdoor-intent 41.3%, existing-customers 68.8%, team-intent 82.4%. The team-intent sequence has the highest engagement quality.
mmai newsletter traffic is negligible — only 1 session from 33 events, suggesting mostly bot/crawler activity or a single low-engagement visit.
Bounce rate improvement: Overall bounce rate dropped from 7.34% to 5.56% — a 1.78pp improvement. The Existing Customers sequence is the star at 0.37% bounce rate.
SMS channel: 2,272 SMS sent with 99.91% delivery (only 2 failures). No new SMS sends this period — the SMS step was completed in the prior period.
Open rate decline (12.81% → 10.79%) is expected as campaigns mature and reach later-step contacts who are less engaged. Step-3 open rates are 8-9% across all sequences.
Click rate improved (+0.25pp to 0.84%), driven by the Existing Customers email sequence which has a 4.06% click rate on Email Step 1.
Anonymous Visitors sequence was paused during this period. Its 20.33% bounce rate was the highest across all sequences.
The new MailChimp sequence was created June 9 but has 0 members — the P&P_MailChimp+May2026New_Customers list (2,393 leads) is ready but not yet imported.
5 of 8 recent customer orders (May 1–June 21) are not in any platform list or sequence — these are missed re-engagement opportunities.
nextSteps: Import P&P_MailChimp+May2026New_Customers list into the MailChimp sequence to activate matched customers.
Add 5 unmatched customers (Kofsky, Penkwitt, Woodberry, Nguyen, Madej) to the platform — either as a new list or appended to the existing customer database.
Consider adding UTM-tagged links with key event tracking to sequence emails — currently 0 key events attributed to any campaign.
Evaluate whether to unpause the Anonymous Visitors sequence or retire it given 20.33% bounce rate.
